messages.content: 從一顆距離地球4光年的恆星發出的光需要多少時間才能抵達地球？

function.name: light_travel_time
function.description: Calculate the time taken for light to travel from a celestial body to another. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

distance_in_light_years.description: The distance between the two celestial bodies in light years.

speed_of_light.description: The speed of light in vacuum, in m/s. Default value is 299792458 m/s.

So we can call with distance_in_light_years: 4. It will compute time? The function likely returns time in seconds? So we can call it. The output likely is time in seconds or maybe years. But we can compute manually: 4 light years = 4 years. So answer: 4 years. If we want seconds: 4 * (365.25 days/year * 24 * 3600) = about 126,230,400 seconds? Wait compute: 1 year ~ 31557600 seconds. 4 years ~ 126230400 seconds. Actually 31557600 * 4 = 126230400. So answer: 4 years or 126 million seconds. Let's call function.
